# vicciz

> vicciz is a travel-technology company building Kiipling, an AI agent for
> travel agencies coordinating disrupted trips. It connects affected bookings,
> prepares provider requests and tracks replies across hotels, transfers,
> tours and activities.

The service is designed for trip care under the agency's own brand. The
traveller or agency operator reviews each proposed message before it is sent.
Booking changes depend on provider confirmation. Cases that need a person can
be handed to an operator.

Last updated: 2026-10-20.

## Product focus

- **Cross-vendor incident coordination.** Connect a flight disruption to the
  hotel check-in, transfer pickup and activities it affects. Keep provider
  requests and replies in the same case.
- **Provider outreach without provider API integrations.** Travel businesses
  connect trip data through an API. Hotels, transfer companies and tour
  operators are contacted over WhatsApp and email without needing their own
  API integration.

## Pilot focus

The first white-label pilot focuses on small agencies running Kivrey Tsadikim
pilgrimage tours, coordinating flight disruptions with hotel and ground-transport
bookings, with operator takeover available.

The pilot needs to establish:

- Confirmed resolution: cases that reach a confirmed outcome with providers,
  and requests that remain unresolved.
- Operator effort: time spent reviewing, following up and taking over cases.
- Time to recovery: time from disruption detection to a confirmed outcome,
  including provider response time.
- Cost per resolved case: service and messaging costs plus operator time,
  compared with the agency's own handling costs for similar cases.

These are pilot success measures. No measured resolution rate or cost saving
is published on this page.

## Commercial terms and access

- Priority audience: online travel agencies, travel agents and tour operators.
- Target pricing: $8–15 per resolved incident, to be validated in pilots.
  Pricing, commercial terms and the definition of resolution are agreed with
  each business.
- Agency access: contact neryar@vicciz.com to discuss supported trip types,
  provider channels, operator handoff and success measures.
- Traveller access: the vicciz app and forwarded booking confirmations provide
  routes to share trip details. Contact vicciz about availability and supported
  trip types.
- Channels: WhatsApp and email; voice planned. Setup and availability are
  agreed for each pilot.
- Application hosting: Google Cloud Run in europe-west3 (Frankfurt).
  PostgreSQL persistence: eu-central-1. Both are EU regions.

## How the agent works

1. Monitor flight-status signals against the booked itinerary.
2. Identify affected bookings and prioritise requests needing attention.
3. Draft provider requests using booking details, available terms and relevant
   passenger-rights rules such as EU261 and US DOT regulations.
4. Present each proposed message for traveller or agency-operator approval.
5. Send approved requests, track provider replies and surface unresolved items
   for an operator. Booking changes depend on provider confirmation.
